author: Chapin Jewell News & Tribune Correspondent
title: Keyser beats Petersburg and Berkeley Springs with pair of 3-2 wins | Mineral County WV News and Tribune | wvnews.com
text:
KEYSER, W.Va. (WV News) – After starting the season with a split in their first two games against Preston (win) and Moorefield (loss), Keyser moved to 3-1 overall with a pair of 3-2 victories over Petersburg at home, and Berkeley Springs on the road.
Keyser 3, Petersburg 2
In what can best be described as a come from behind thriller, Keyser first fell behind Peterburg in sets one and two by scores of 25-17 and 25-19. With their backs against the wall, therefore, the Lady Tornado crawled back, winning set three, 25-23, and set four, 25-20, to tie the match at two sets apiece. Then, in the deciding fifth and final set, the Lady Tornado earned a close, 17-15 victory, winning them the match, 3-2.
Bella Haines had 13 assists, four kills, one dig, and one block; Keyser Kesner earned nine assists, six kills, and two digs; Sophie Lambka had six kills and two digs; Amirah Bryant had six kills; Jillian Ault had six kills, one dig, and three blocks; Aubrey Fisher had dour kills, one dig, and two blocks; Libby Del Signore had four digs; Nakira Bartlett had three digs.; Brooklyn Lesher had one dig.
“In that third set, we were going right at them. I told the girls, we have to play smarter. Basically, we had to place the ball. We had to find a couple of weaknesses and we found about three of them on that side, and we pointed them out, and we went right at them,” Keyser coach Brian Kesner stated.
According to Kesner, “These girls work very hard. They’re young, but we communicate so well, and they work so well together. It’s hard to keep them focused sometimes, but they do play hard, and they do work hard.”
It was a match in which a young team gained valuable experience and learned how to win.
“Right there, No. 7, Sophie Lambka, she was a key player tonight. She’s the one that got us a few points when we needed the points and got us the win. She’s a freshman. She’s 14 years old. She plays great. She doesn’t play like a 14-year old, she plays like a senior. I’m very proud of her, and I’m very proud of the whole team.” Kesner noted.
Keyser 3, Berkeley Springs 2
Against Berkeley Springs, Keyser was able to earn another 3-2 victory, earning a win the fifth and deciding set by a tally of 15-9.
Amirah Bryant had 13 kills and two blocks; Sophie Lambka had 10 kills, one block, and one dig; Kiya Kesner had three aces, three kills, 15 assists, and three digs; Bella Haines had one ace, two kills, and 18 assists; Jillian Ault had one ace, 13 kills, two assists, three blocks, and one dig; Aubrey Fisher had four aces, four kills, and one dig; Libby Del Signore had 12 digs; Nakira Bartlett had nine digs; Brooklyn Lesher had one ace, one kill, and three digs.
“Berkeley Springs all-around was a very solid team, and well-coached. I’m starting to think my team has to lose a set before they start to play. This was another great come from behind win. This team just doesn’t give up,” Kesner noted.
According to Kesner, “We moved the ball around up front. Sophomore Amirah Bryant had a huge night with 12 kills. Freshman Sophie Lambka contributed 10 kills and was very solid on defense. Jillian Ault continues to do what Jillian does up front with 13 kills and three blocks.”
“Overall, our success is due to a complete team effort. They work together so well. They are constantly analyzing every play on how we can get better,” Kesner stated.
What’s next?
Keyser (3-1) will next host Calvary Chapel Christian Academy on Thursday, Sep. 4 at 7:15 p.m.
